label: text
text: General Hortzog, Nationalist Premier of South Africa, arrived in London to-day to attend the Imperial Conference.

label: text
text: To representatives of the Press he made a notable statement. He wished to assure the people of Great Britain that at the Conference the Union of South Africa had no wish to be anything but a helpful associate in advancing the interests of the British community of nations.

label: text
text:
"We intend to apply ourselves to the task of the Conference in a spirit of co-operation, seeking by united action to promote the common interests of us all. One of the main tasks—if not the main task—with which the Conference will be confronted will be to have co-operation between the members of the States of the British Empire placed on a more certain and satisfactory basis. If success in that respect is to result from our labours, questions of a fundamental nature affecting Empire relations, both domestic and foreign as well, have to be grappled with and decided. Fortunately there is nothing revolutionary in any of these questions—nothing that is not in fullest harmony with the basis already laid down. Given goodwill, courage, and faith we ought to be able to accomplish much that will ensure permanency and harmony in all our relations in the future."
Accompanying the Premier were Mr. Havenga, Minister of Finance, Mr. Heddon, head of the Customs, and Sir Henry Hoy, General Manager of the South African Railways. British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: The sudden appearance of coast-guards at Bayway, New Jersey, caused a scuttle of a crew unloading the cargo of a large British steam trawler, which, the officials describe as an old rum-running offender.

label: text
text: It apparently sailed through the coastguard fleet, eluded the police boats, and had unloaded 1,000 out 2,000 cases of liquor on board before the coastguard arrived and took possession.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text:
A delayed despatch from Changsha, dated September 29, which has just reached the American Legation, reports the capture of three American missionaries by bandits at Maliwan in West Hunan, namely, Cal. Beck and Minerva Wall, both of the Reformed Church, and Lewis Koebbe, of the Evangelist Church.
The State Department has been informed, and steps are being taken to secure a release—Ruter

label: text
text: Work has been brought "to a standstill" at Tilbury Docks in consequence of a lightning strike of 2,200 dockers. "Thirteen steamers, including food ships, are idle."

label: text
text: The dispute is due to the Port of London Authorities refusing a permit to Mr. Attwood, the Trade Union Branch Secretary, to enter the docks.

label: text
text: Resentment in the connection has been smouldering since the ban was imposed after the general strike in May. The Union did not ask the men to strike and the men are not willing to obey Mr. Attwood's repeated appeals to resume work.

label: text
text: The principal ships in dock are the Orient Line's "Osterley" and the P. & O. "Kashmir", "Cathay" and "China." — Reuter

label: text
text: The dockers leader, Mr. Thompson, at the conclusion of an interview with the shipowners at Tilbury declared that he had received an understanding that the Port of London Authority would call a meeting to discuss the grievance. Meantime he had recommended the men to return, but was unable to guarantee that the men would obey.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Nearly 9,000 more miners resumed work to-day, 7,000 of them being in the counties of Nottingham and Derbyshire, where the Districts Executives have recommended the acceptance of the Government's proposals.

label: text
text: It is authentically stated that the total number of persons employed at the pits producing coal was to-day 171,419.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Two colonels, leaders in the mutiny of the Republican Guard on September 9, have been sentenced to life imprisonment.—Router.

A five-days week for all workers is declared to be the definite goal of the Federation of Labour at the final meeting of the Executive Council prior to the 46th annual Convention to be opened to day.
This policy will be recommended to the affiliated organisations as the basis of negotiation for renewal of contracts with employers.

Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: Hakodate messages state that a Soviet steamer arrived recently from Wrangel Island where she landed fifty emigrants, whilst three aviators surveyed the island from the air.

label: text
text: It is alleged that the members of the expedition removed the British and American flags, which had been planted there, substituting their own.—Reuter.
